premise: The existing authenticated Node service pipe identifies one service instance, while design 37 operations must distinguish user, lead, and seat authority across concurrent sessions.
logic_check: A target ID or caller value selected by Node or model does not prove the request's originating seat. Native-owned I/O origin can be bound to a principal, seat, domain, generation, and current grant before the operation is accepted.
rule: The v37 request wire does not contain caller or grant fields.
The host records the originating user or seat channel and derives caller for each operation from that native-owned binding.

A Node-forwarded invocation, if used, refers only to one host-observed call and is bound to the complete request bytes, source, generation, and host epoch; Node cannot choose a reusable seat identity.

Writes check current grant, revocation, scope, policy revision, target revision, mutation, and receipt within the existing verified database connection. Scoped reads, replay, and delivery recheck current authority.
The existing R2 service capability continues to authenticate the service only and is never promoted to a user, lead, or seat grant.
Until native origin binding exists, v37 ingress rejects without a success receipt, database write, or process launch.
existing_composition: ProductDatabase already delegates the same verified connection, OwnerIssuer, and ProcessCustodian to store/session.rs. No change to product_database.rs is currently required.
falsifiable_checks: Two simultaneous seat channels retain distinct native caller identity when their requests interleave.
Changing target ID or swapping a forwarded invocation does not change caller and is denied outside its grant.
A direct request on the old Node service pipe cannot perform user-only or seat-only v37 operations.
Revocation, generation change, and host restart invalidate old authority before a new write or delivery.
Legacy R2 frames and stop custody retain their prior behavior.
